newsitem.title: JAPAN: PHILIPS JOINS SONY, SHARP IN PDP PANEL DEVELOPMENT.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS JOINS SONY, SHARP IN PDP PANEL DEVELOPMENT.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Wednesday that Philips Electronics NV of the Netherlands has joined Sony and Sharp Corp in the development of plasma display panels (PDPs), a new generation of flat television screens.
The three companies will start development work this autumn and are planning to demonstrate a 40-inch flat screen before the end of this year, a Sony spokesman said.
Details on investments in new facilities and the timing of product launches have not yet been decided, he said.

A plasma display is a flat panel used for computer and television screens. Unlike conventional displays, PDP technology allows for larger screens without an increase in weight or thickness, making it suitable for compact multimedia displays and televisions that can hang on the wall.
Sony's PDP uses PALC (plasma-addressed liquid crystal) technology developed by Tektronix Inc of the U.S.
Sony sub-licensed its technology to Sharp last September when Sharp agreed to collaborate with Sony in the development of PALC panels.
Philips will license the technology from Tektronix, the Sony spokesman said.
Fujitsu Ltd , Matsushita Electric Industrial Co and NEC Corp are also engaged in the development of PDPs using technologies that differ from Sony's.
